figs.title: Steepest descent, CG and Newton
figs.caption: On a quadratic with exact line searches, steepest descent zigzags with each step orthogonal to the previous one, conjugate gradient reaches x* in n = 2 steps, and Newton reaches x* in one step. Larger condition numbers make the steepest descent zigzag longer.

figs.title: Surrogate fit quality
figs.caption: A model with too few terms underfits and carries high bias, while a degree 7 polynomial through 8 points interpolates the noise and oscillates between samples. The cubic balances bias and variance, which cross validation error identifies.

figs.title: Convexity definitions
figs.caption: A convex function lies on or below every chord, f(θx + (1 − θ)y) ≤ θf(x) + (1 − θ)f(y). A differentiable convex function lies on or above every tangent, so any stationary point is a global minimum.

figs.title: DSM and central composite design
figs.caption: In an N² matrix, marks below the diagonal are feedback couplings that force iteration, and reordering the disciplines reduces them. A central composite design adds axial points at ±α and a center point to the 2ᵏ factorial corners so a full quadratic can be fit.

figs.title: Static stability and static margin
figs.caption: Static longitudinal stability requires dC_m/dα < 0 together with C_m0 > 0 so the aircraft trims at a positive α. The slope dC_m/dα equals −C_Lα times the static margin, the distance from the CG to the neutral point in chords.

figs.title: High lift devices
figs.caption: A trailing edge flap adds camber, shifting the lift curve up and α₀ to more negative values with a higher C_Lmax at a lower stall angle. A leading edge slat keeps the flow attached to a higher stall angle, extending the linear range to a higher C_Lmax.

figs.title: Von Mises and Tresca yield surfaces
figs.caption: In plane stress the von Mises surface is an ellipse and the Tresca surface is a hexagon inscribed in it, touching at the uniaxial and equibiaxial points. In pure shear, Tresca predicts yield at σ_Y/2 and von Mises at σ_Y/√3.

figs.caption: For a section with I_yz ≠ 0, a moment about z bends the beam about a neutral axis inclined at β with tan β = I_yz/I_yy. Bending about a principal axis alone gives a neutral axis along that same axis.

figs.title: Neo-Hookean balloon limit point
figs.caption: For a thin neo-Hookean balloon the pressure follows λ⁻¹ − λ⁻⁷, peaking at λ = 7^(1/6) ≈ 1.38, while the uniaxial Cauchy stress μ(λ² − 1/λ) rises monotonically. The limit point comes from the geometry of thinning and growing radius.

figs.title: Reference and current configurations
figs.caption: The motion x = χ(X, t) maps each material point X of B₀ to its current position x in B, and the deformation gradient maps material line elements as dx = F dX with J = det F > 0. Lagrangian fields are written in X and Eulerian fields in x.

figs.title: Voigt and Reuss bounds
figs.caption: The Voigt equal strain rule of mixtures is the upper bound and the Reuss equal stress rule is the lower bound on composite stiffness. Voigt approximates the longitudinal fiber direction modulus and Reuss approximates the transverse modulus.
